judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's arithmetic claims are exact: f(3)=7; 4x-5=19 -> x=6; g(2)=1 from the table (1,4),(2,1),(3,5),(4,2),(5,3); f(2+3)=f(5)=15 against Jo's f(2)+f(3)=3+7=10; 3+2.5m=28 -> m=10; g(4)=2 < B(4)=5; 30-6x=12 -> x=3. The judge is also right that problem 8 is properly declared {'type': 'manual'} and that the packet consistently labels which quantity is input and which is output. But 'manual' was applied to exactly one of five open components. Problem 3 says 'Explain in one sentence what Priya's method actually computes', problem 5 says 'Explain why C(28) answers the wrong question' and problem 7 says 'Circle the first line where Marcus goes wrong, say what he swapped' - a marked representation plus a written diagnosis - and all three are recorded as plain single-value entries. The answer key knows they are open: problem 3's solution ends 'Accept any wording that says Priya searched the output row instead of the input row'. Problem 4 also prints two requested values ('Compute f(2+3) correctly, and state the value Jo's method would give instead'); verify.json id 4 expects 15 only - the 10 exists solely as a trap, i.e. declared as a value the check must reject, which is the inverse of what the student is asked to supply. Finally the Quick Answers bank prints '6. ---' although verify.json id 6 has the verified relation '<'.

strengths_to_preserve: Seven declared traps, each machine-proved distinguishable from the correct value and each named in plain language in the 'Common wrong answers' block: 2 (solving when you should substitute), 71 (f(19)), 4 (reading the table backwards), 10 (splitting f(2+3) additively), 21 (multiplying the outputs), 73 (C(28)) and -42 (h(12)). This is exactly what the prompt's 'declare any planted wrong results as machine-checked misconception traps' asks for.

Problems 1 and 2 are the same rule run in both directions on the same function (f(3) = 7, then find x with f(x) = 19), which makes the evaluate-versus-solve contrast the sheet's spine rather than a remark.

Problem 8 is correctly declared manual with a descriptive 'desc' field, and the build honestly exits 2 and says so - the right outcome for an open response and the pattern the other cases in this shard should copy.

root_causes.description: Manual declaration is treated as a per-problem property rather than a per-response one. A problem that asks for a diagnosis AND a value gets whichever single entry the author wrote, so the diagnosis half disappears from the verification record even when the answer key openly grades it by judgment.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 3 requires a one-sentence explanation plus g(2); verify.json id 3 is a single read_data entry expecting 1.
worksheet.pdf problem 7 requires circling a line and naming the swap plus the input; verify.json id 7 is a single eval expecting 3.
answer_key.pdf problem 3 prints 'Accept any wording that says Priya searched the output row instead of the input row' - grader judgment against a machine-verified id.

root_causes.description: A value the student is explicitly asked to produce can be declared only as a trap, which records it as a value the check must reject. Problem 4 asks for both the correct result and the result Jo's method gives, and the second is represented by the trap machinery rather than by an answer entry.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 4: 'Compute f(2 + 3) correctly, and state the value Jo's method would give instead.'
verify.json id 4: expected 15, with 10 appearing only under 'traps'.
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers prints '4. 15' for a two-value question.

root_causes.description: render_quick_answers cannot render a relational expected value, so problem 6's verified '<' prints as the em-dash reserved for manual-only items - the same glyph problem 8 (genuinely manual) gets.
evidence: answer_key.pdf Quick Answers: '6. ---' and '8. ---' are indistinguishable although only 8 is manual.
scripts/render_quick_answers.py _fmt returns '---' when sympify fails on the string.

improvements.title: Declare the diagnosis halves of problems 3, 5 and 7 as manual companions
improvements.proposed_change: Allow (and require) a manual entry alongside a machine entry on the same id when the problem asks for both a value and a written or marked response. Add manual companions to ids 3, 5 and 7 here, and lint worksheet.tex problem bodies for 'explain', 'say what', 'name the', 'circle' so the omission fails the build instead of passing silently.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ with a fixture problem whose statement contains an open-response verb ("explain", "name the error", "describe", "circle") and whose verify JSON has no matching manual entry, and assert the build reports an unflagged open response. It fails today (the fixture builds green with exit 0) and passes after the lint lands.
improvements.expected_impact: Error-analysis sheets stop reporting themselves as fully machine verified when the graded skill is a written diagnosis; the manual-review count in the delivery message becomes accurate.
improvements.risk: Over-flagging turns every sheet into a manual-review pile. Scope the lint to imperatives that own an answer slot and let an author suppress a false positive explicitly.

improvements.title: Problem 4 asks for two values; only f(2+3) = 15 is verified
improvements.proposed_change: Add a second entry on id 4 with expected 10 for 'the value Jo's method would give', keeping the trap declaration separately if the intent is also to reject 10 as an answer to the first part. Generally: when a trap value is also a requested response, it must appear as an answer entry, not only as a trap.
improvements.regression_test: Add a gate case to tests/ that loads a fixture worksheet whose problem prints N distinct requested responses and a verify JSON covering fewer of them, and assert the build fails with a slot-coverage error. It fails today (no such check exists, so the fixture builds green) and passes once the answer-slot declaration is enforced.
improvements.expected_impact: The bank line for problem 4 becomes '15, 10' and both numbers a student writes are bound to recomputed values.
improvements.risk: Declaring the same number as both an expected answer and a trap could confuse the trap distinguishability check; the two declarations must be scoped to their own response, not to the problem.

improvements.title: Quick Answers shows problem 6's verified '<' as the manual-item em-dash
improvements.proposed_change: Render relational expected values ('<', '>', '=', '<=', '>=') as their math-mode symbols in the bank, and reserve '---' for ids with no expected value at all. Problem 6 should read 'g(4) < B(4)' or at minimum '$<$'.
improvements.regression_test: Extend tests/test_render_quick_answers.py with two cases: a compare entry of order "relation" with expected ">", and a system entry with expected [] (no solution). Assert the rendered bank lines read "$>$" and "no solution" rather than "---". Both assertions fail against the current _fmt/render_entry and pass after the fix.
improvements.expected_impact: A teacher can tell a verified comparison answer from a genuinely open item at a glance, on this sheet and every other sheet with a compare item.

case_summary: A sharply focused error-analysis packet: every mistake on the sheet is one number in the wrong slot, four named students carry realistic wrong work, and all seven arithmetic results recompute correctly. The trap declarations are the best in my slice - seven planted wrong values, each machine-proved distinguishable and each explained in the 'Common wrong answers' block - and problem 8 is correctly declared manual with the build honestly exiting 2. The gap is that manual was applied once where it was needed four or five times: problems 3, 5 and 7 all demand a written diagnosis (and problem 7 a circled line) yet are recorded as single machine-verified values, and problem 4 asks for two numbers while only one is an answer entry. A minor renderer defect prints problem 6's verified '<' as the same em-dash used for manual problem 8.
